<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8`, an opt-in MLA prefill backend that runs AITER's FlyDSL FP8 flash attention on dynamically per-tensor quantized Q/K/V, for Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950). Port of the approach in [ROCm/ATOM#2191](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2191); supersedes #62447, which its author closed in favor of this PR.

## Claims

- New tokens, context chunks and context-free prefills all run FP8 FlyDSL attention. Selected with `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`; not auto-selected.
- Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 agentic replay (InferenceX agentx-mvp, c48): total throughput +4.5%, TTFT p90 -15.8%, ITL p90 -8.7%.
- 8K fresh prefill on current main and AITER v0.1.27, against the ASM FP8 prefill it replaces: TTFT mean -2.5%, p90 -9.1%.
- Accuracy unchanged. With DSpark MTP on current main: GPQA Diamond 91.4% in both arms, RULER NIAH 100% at 32K and 128K in both arms, DSpark acceptance length 3.819 vs 3.823, GSM8K 0.9651 vs 0.9591 (within one standard error of the difference). Earlier revision, without MTP: GSM8K 0.9621 in both arms; Kimi tool-call eval within run-to-run noise.
- No model or shape is hard-coded: availability and head dims come from AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported`; inputs the kernel cannot take (empty, or at least 2^31 elements) fall back to the parent BF16 `ROCM_AITER_FA` path.

## Validation

Unit tests, MI355X, main @ `410ab341a8` + this PR:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py        # 935 passed, 349 skipped (GLM dims, TRTLLM-only params)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_flydsl_fp8_prefill.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py   # 64 passed (kernel tests included)
```

`ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` is in `PREFILL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST`, so `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` check it against SDPA; a `context_free_prefill` spec checks context-free batches against SDPA with this backend selected. That spec checks output only: it also passes with `_asm_fp8_prefill_superseded` forced to `False`, so it does not show which kernel ran; the e2e runs below confirm the backend from the server log.

CI coverage: only the MI355 `test_mla_backends.py` step runs with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, so it is the one CI job that exercises this backend. The FlyDSL kernel test and the head-dim selector test skip in CI (the `kernels/attention` step runs on MI300/gfx942, and the selector step does not enable AITER); I ran them on MI355X above.

End-to-end, 8x MI355X. Server (InferenceX `kimik3_fp4_mi355x` config; the arms differ only in `mla_prefill_backend`):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
# baseline: --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' (ASM FP8 prefill for context-free batches)
```

| Benchmark | Command | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot (strict / flexible) | `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5` | 0.9621 / 0.9621 | 0.9621 / 0.9621 |
| Agentic replay, c48, 3600 s | `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --concurrency 48 --benchmark-duration 3600 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126` | 91,787 tok/s, TTFT p90 3690 ms | 95,931 tok/s, TTFT p90 3106 ms |
| 8K fresh prefill x128, c16, 2 runs | `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 16` | TTFT mean 6414 ms, p90 7303 ms | TTFT mean 6255 ms, p90 6638 ms |

Accuracy with DSpark MTP, current main + this PR at `4d1ee17353` (code identical to `aea6855e4d`), AITER v0.1.27. Same server plus `--speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'`; one run per arm.

| Benchmark | Command | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GPQA Diamond, 198 questions | `evalscope eval --eval-type openai_api --datasets gpqa_diamond --eval-batch-size 32 --generation-config '{"max_tokens": 100000, "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95}' --seed 42` | 91.4% | 91.4% |
| RULER NIAH, 8 `niah_*` tasks x 50 samples per length | `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks niah_single_1,...,niah_multivalue --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[32768,131072]}'` | 100% / 100% (32K / 128K) | 100% / 100% (32K / 128K) |
| GSM8K 5-shot (strict / flexible) | as above | 0.9651 / 0.9651 | 0.9591 / 0.9591 |
| DSpark acceptance length / rate, over the GSM8K run | `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters | 3.819 / 0.705 (35,781 drafts) | 3.823 / 0.706 (35,608 drafts) |

The GSM8K gap is 8 of 1319 questions, 0.8 standard errors of the difference (per-arm stderr 0.51% / 0.55%), so it is within noise. NIAH uses lm-eval's RULER generator with 50 samples per task and length instead of 500, and both arms read the same generated samples.

<details><summary>Run details and more results</summary>

- The 8K row and the unit tests use current main with AITER v0.1.27. The GSM8K and agentic rows were measured on the first revision of this PR (same kernel calls behind an env flag, AITER 0.1.22 with the FlyDSL FP8 sources from AITER main); `cross_seqlen=True` since then is bit-identical.
- Full server command and environment:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --load-format fastsafetensors --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}' --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":96,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,3,...,96]}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}' \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a
```
- Agentic replay, full table:

| Metric | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 1176 / 3690 / 22443 | 1119 / 3106 / 16155 |
| ITL p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 51.1 / 74.6 / 188.0 | 49.2 / 68.2 / 130.5 |
| Total / output tok/s | 91,787 / 609.2 | 95,931 / 638.5 |

- Kimi Vendor Verifier `kimi_tool_call_schema_full` (408 records), two runs per arm: baseline 0.9779 / 0.9877, FlyDSL 0.9755 / 0.9951.
- Prefill TTFT, first revision: 32K chunked -1.6%, 128K -7.3%, 64K with a 56K cached prefix -6.2%.
- Backend micro-benchmark (12 heads, qk 192 / v 128, FP8 time includes quantization), BF16 vs FlyDSL: 1x8192 causal 313 vs 229 us; q 1024 + context 64K 1278 vs 549 us; q 128 + context 64K 1251 vs 351 us.

</details>

## Details

- **Backend.** Subclasses `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Q is quantized once per forward and reused by every context chunk; each chunk quantizes only its own K/V. The LSE layout is unchanged, so `merge_attn_states` is reused.
- **Context-free prefills.** With this backend selected, `ROCM_AITER_MLA` no longer runs its ASM FP8 prefill (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd`) or allocates its PS workspace; the gate is `_asm_fp8_prefill_superseded`, shared by the metadata builder and `forward_mha`.
- **Quantizer.** `triton_per_tensor_fp8_quant.py`, adapted from ATOM#2191's fused QKV quantizer (MIT), quantizes up to three strided tensors in two launches with no atomics and no recompiles across batch shapes. Existing ops do not fit: `ops.scaled_fp8_quant` matches numerically but takes the per-row path on strided V (65K tokens: 10.2 ms for Q/K/V vs 0.35 ms here), and `rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` returns wrong results on strided V.
- **Docs.** `mla_prefill_backend`'s docstring, which renders the CLI reference, now lists the ROCm prefill backends.
- **AITER.** Needs `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported` (ROCm/aiter#5718); main's pinned AITER v0.1.27 has it, along with `softmax_scale`, short-query split-K and the AOT `varlen_cross` kernels for `kimi_k3_tp8` (ROCm/aiter#5796, #5901). The new-token call uses `cross_seqlen=True` so it hits those AOT kernels; output is bit-identical to `cross_seqlen=False`.
- **Not a duplicate.** #62447 (same idea inside `ROCM_AITER_FA`) is closed in favor of this PR. #51551 is a gfx942 Gluon path with static per-head scales.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8 MLA prefill backend.
+
+Checks the fused per-tensor FP8 quantization against a torch reference, and the
+backend's FP8 new-token and context-chunk attention (including long contexts
+and Q reuse) against the BF16 ROCM_AITER_FA backend. End-to-end correctness
+against SDPA is covered in tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py.
+"""
+
+import math
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("ROCm-only test", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill import aiter_flydsl_fp8  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.aiter_flash_attn import (  # noqa: E402
+    AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.aiter_flydsl_fp8 import (  # noqa: E402
+    AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.base import MLADimensions  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.selector import (  # noqa: E402
+    MLAPrefillSelectorConfig,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_per_tensor_fp8_quant import (  # noqa: E402
+    _BLOCK,
+    _PARTS,
+    fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant,
+)
+
+NUM_HEADS = 12
+QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM = 128
+QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM = 64
+V_HEAD_DIM = 128
+KV_LORA_RANK = 512
+QK_HEAD_DIM = QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM
+FP8_DTYPE = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+
+
+def _reference_quant(x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    amax = x.abs().float().max() if x.numel() else x.new_zeros((), dtype=torch.float)
+    descale = amax / torch.finfo(FP8_DTYPE).max if amax > 0 else amax.new_tensor(1e-6)
+    x_fp8 = (x.float() / descale).clamp(-448, 448).to(FP8_DTYPE)
+    return x_fp8, descale.reshape(1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [0, 1, 37, 8192])
+def test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_matches_reference(num_tokens: int) -> None:
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda") * 4
+    k = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda")
+    kv = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + V_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda"
+    )
+    # V is a strided view of the kv_b_proj output, as in MLA prefill.
+    v = kv[..., QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM:]
+    inputs = [x.to(torch.bfloat16) for x in (q, k, v)]
+    outputs, descales = fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(*inputs)
+    for x, x_fp8, descale in zip(inputs, outputs, descales):
+        ref_fp8, ref_descale = _reference_quant(x)
+        assert x_fp8.shape == x.shape and x_fp8.is_contiguous()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(descale, ref_descale, rtol=1e-6, atol=0)
+        # x * (1 / descale) may round one e4m3 step away from x / descale.
+        ulp_diff = x_fp8.view(torch.int8).int() - ref_fp8.view(torch.int8).int()
+        assert ulp_diff.numel() == 0 or ulp_diff.abs().max() <= 1
+
+
+_STRIPE = _PARTS * _BLOCK
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "numel",
+    [1, _BLOCK, _BLOCK + 1, _STRIPE - 1, _STRIPE, _STRIPE + 1, 3 * _STRIPE + 7],
+)
+def test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_covers_every_element(numel: int) -> None:
+    """One grid serves inputs of different sizes; no element may be dropped."""
+    x = torch.full((numel, 1, 1), 0.5, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    expected = 100.0 / torch.finfo(FP8_DTYPE).max
+    for pos in sorted({0, _BLOCK - 1, _BLOCK, _STRIPE - 1, _STRIPE, numel - 1}):
+        if pos >= numel:
+            continue
+        probe = x.clone()
+        probe[pos] = 100.0
+        _, (descale,) = fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(probe)
+        assert descale.item() == pytest.approx(expected), f"missed element {pos}"
+
+
+def test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_zero_input() -> None:
+    x = torch.zeros(4, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    (x_fp8,), (descale,) = fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(x)
+    assert descale.item() > 0
+    assert x_fp8.float().abs().max().item() == 0
+
+
+def _make_backend(backend_cls, v_head_dim: int = V_HEAD_DIM):
+    vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(model_config=SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+    return backend_cls(
+        num_heads=NUM_HEADS,
+        scale=1.0 / math.sqrt(QK_HEAD_DIM),
+        kv_lora_rank=KV_LORA_RANK,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM,
+        v_head_dim=v_head_dim,
+        vllm_config=vllm_config,
+    )
+
+
+def _selector_config(v_head_dim: int) -> MLAPrefillSelectorConfig:
+    return MLAPrefillSelectorConfig(
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        mla_dimensions=MLADimensions(
+            qk_nope_head_dim=QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM,
+            qk_rope_head_dim=QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM,
+            v_head_dim=v_head_dim,
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _skip_if_unsupported() -> None:
+    reasons = AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend.validate_configuration(
+        current_platform.get_device_capability(), _selector_config(V_HEAD_DIM)
+    )
+    if reasons:
+        pytest.skip(f"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8 unavailable: {reasons}")
+
+
+def _cu_seqlens(lens: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.tensor([0, *torch.tensor(lens).cumsum(0).tolist()]).to(
+        device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+
+
+def _assert_close_to_bf16(fp8_result, bf16_result) -> None:
+    fp8_out, fp8_lse = fp8_result
+    bf16_out, bf16_lse = bf16_result
+    # FP8 error scales with the output, which is far smaller for long context
+    # chunks than for new tokens.
+    atol = 0.1 * bf16_out.abs().max().item()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fp8_out, bf16_out, rtol=0, atol=atol)
+    # FP8 rounding of Q.K dominates rows that attend to only a few keys, so the
+    # elementwise bound is loose; the mean catches a uniform error such as a
+    # wrong Q scale.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fp8_lse, bf16_lse, rtol=0, atol=0.25)
+    assert (fp8_lse - bf16_lse).abs().mean() < 0.01
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "query_lens,context_lens",
+    [([2048], [16384]), ([128], [65536])],
+)
+def test_flydsl_fp8_prefill_matches_bf16(monkeypatch, query_lens, context_lens):
+    _skip_if_unsupported()
+    fp8_backend = _make_backend(AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend)
+    bf16_backend = _make_backend(AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend)
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    num_tokens, num_ctx = sum(query_lens), sum(context_lens)
+    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    k = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + V_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda"
+    ).bfloat16()[..., QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM:]
+    ctx_k = torch.randn(num_ctx, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    ctx_v = torch.randn(num_ctx, NUM_HEADS, V_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+
+    metadata = SimpleNamespace(
+        query_start_loc=_cu_seqlens(query_lens), max_query_len=max(query_lens)
+    )
+    chunk = SimpleNamespace(
+        token_slice=slice(0, num_tokens),
+        query_start_loc=_cu_seqlens(query_lens),
+        cu_seq_lens=_cu_seqlens(context_lens),
+        max_query_len=max(query_lens),
+        max_seq_len=max(context_lens),
+    )
+    quantized_counts: list[int] = []
+
+    def spy_quant(*tensors, **kwargs):
+        quantized_counts.append(len(tensors))
+        return fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(*tensors, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(aiter_flydsl_fp8, "fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant", spy_quant)
+    results = []
+    for backend in (fp8_backend, bf16_backend):
+        backend.prepare_metadata(metadata)
+        new = backend.run_prefill_new_tokens(q, k, v, return_softmax_lse=True)
+        ctx = backend.run_prefill_context_chunk(
+            chunk, q[chunk.token_slice], ctx_k, ctx_v
+        )
+        results.append((new, ctx))
+    # Q is quantized with K/V for the new tokens and reused by the context chunk.
+    assert quantized_counts == [3, 2]
+
+    (fp8_new, fp8_ctx), (bf16_new, bf16_ctx) = results
+    _assert_close_to_bf16(fp8_new, bf16_new)
+    _assert_close_to_bf16(fp8_ctx, bf16_ctx)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Fused dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization of up to three attention inputs.
+
+Each ``[tokens, heads, dim]`` input (possibly strided, e.g. V as a view of the
+``kv_b_proj`` output) gets its own amax and FP32 descale. A partial-amax pass
+and a reduce-and-quantize pass cover all inputs in two launches; the kernel
+boundary is the only global barrier, so no atomics or zero-initialization are
+needed and the ops are CUDA-graph safe. Compile-time specialization does not
+depend on the token counts (only the grid size does), so varying batch shapes
+do not recompile.
+
+One grid covers all the inputs in each launch, so a program can land past the
+end of a smaller input. Such programs do no work and compute no address, and
+every load and store is masked regardless, so no out-of-range pointer is formed
+or dereferenced.
+
+Adapted from the fused QKV quantizer in ROCm/ATOM (atom/model_ops/
+triton_fused_qkv_quant.py, MIT license).
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+_BLOCK = 4096
+_PARTS = 256
+# Descale for all-zero or empty inputs. A positive value keeps downstream
+# attention kernels from producing NaNs.
+_MIN_DESCALE = 1e-6
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _load(X, offsets, N, SHAPE: tl.constexpr, STRIDE: tl.constexpr):
+    heads, dim = SHAPE
+    offsets = offsets.to(tl.int64)
+    physical = (
+        offsets // (heads * dim) * STRIDE[0]
+        + offsets // dim % heads * STRIDE[1]
+        + offsets % dim * STRIDE[2]
+    )
+    return tl.load(X + physical, offsets < N, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _partial_amax(
+    X,
+    Partial,
+    N,
+    SHAPE: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # The grid is fixed at PARTS, so the trip count is per-program: it drops to
+    # zero once this program's stripe starts past the end of this input.
+    start = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK
+    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.float32)
+    for step in range(tl.cdiv(N - start, PARTS * BLOCK)):
+        offsets = start + step * PARTS * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        x = _load(X, offsets, N, SHAPE, STRIDE)
+        acc = tl.maximum(acc, tl.abs(x))
+    tl.store(Partial + tl.program_id(0), tl.max(acc, 0))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _fused_amax_kernel(
+    X0,
+    X1,
+    X2,
+    Partial,
+    N0,
+    N1,
+    N2,
+    SHAPES: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDES: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    idx = tl.program_id(1)
+    if idx == 0:
+        _partial_amax(X0, Partial, N0, SHAPES[0], STRIDES[0], PARTS, BLOCK)
+    elif idx == 1:
+        _partial_amax(X1, Partial + PARTS, N1, SHAPES[1], STRIDES[1], PARTS, BLOCK)
+    else:
+        _partial_amax(X2, Partial + 2 * PARTS, N2, SHAPES[2], STRIDES[2], PARTS, BLOCK)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _quant(
+    X,
+    Y,
+    Partial,
+    Scale,
+    N,
+    SHAPE: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: tl.constexpr,

I compared against the existing kernels first. On MI355X, with 12 heads, q/k 192 and v 128, and V a strided view of the `kv_b_proj` output:
- `rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` returns wrong results for the strided V.
- `ops.scaled_fp8_quant` matches this kernel: descales within 1e-6, values within 1 e4m3 ulp. It is much slower here, though:

| Tokens | This kernel (Q/K/V, one call) | `scaled_fp8_quant` ×3 | ×3, V made contiguous first |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 50 µs | 189 µs | 59 µs |
| 8,192 | 50 µs | 1,318 µs | 237 µs |
| 65,536 | 352 µs | 10,165 µs | 1,306 µs |

Why it is slower:
- It takes one 2D tensor per call, so Q/K/V need 3 × (memset + amax + quant).
- V's row stride sends it down the per-row path: one 256-thread block and one `atomicMax` per 128-element row, and there are T×H rows. At 65K tokens, V alone takes 9.3 ms there versus 110 µs here.
- An all-zero input gets descale 0.

This kernel is adapted from ATOM's fused QKV quantizer. The one change is that token counts are runtime args, so varying batch shapes don't recompile.

I'd be happy to move it somewhere more general, or to fix the strided path of `dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant` in a follow-up, if you prefer.

> Nice work!
> 
> **Suggestions**:
> 
> 1. Can we create a standalone mla prefill backend for this? there's a lot of useful existing infra for this
> 2. Can we plug that new backend into the existing attention correctness tests?

hi @simondanielsson , thanks for your review! Here are the updates regarding your concerns:
1. **Standalone backend.** The FlyDSL FP8 path now lives in its own prefill backend, `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/aiter_flydsl_fp8.py`). It subclasses `AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend`, so the few inputs FlyDSL can't take fall back to the parent's BF16 path. `ROCM_AITER_FA` is back to its `main` version.
   - Select it with `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`. The env var is gone.
   - Gating goes through the standard hooks:
     - `supported_dtypes = [bf16]`.
     - `supports_compute_capability` requires gfx950.
     - `is_available` requires AITER and the FlyDSL FP8 API.
     - `validate_configuration` defers to AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported` for the head dims.
   - An explicit but unsupported selection therefore fails at startup, instead of silently running BF16 as before.
   - The backend is not in the ROCm auto-selection priorities.
2. **Correctness tests.** The backend is added to `PREFILL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST` in `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py`, so `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` run it against the SDPA reference.
   - GLM dims (v=256) are skipped at collection through `validate_configuration`.
   - The tolerance is loosened for this backend only: `rtol=2**-4, atol=0.3`. With per-tensor e4m3 Q/K/V, a row that attends to only a few tokens is off by up to about 2⁻⁴·max|V|. The largest observed diff was about 0.25.
   - I also added a `context_free_prefill` spec to `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness`, which this backend runs. It covers the builder change that stops `ROCM_AITER_MLA`'s ASM FP8 prefill from bypassing the selected prefill backend.
   - Registry and selector unit tests are added as well.
   - Result on MI355X with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k ROCM_AITER` → 869 passed and 296 skipped. Three `ROCM_AITER_FA` cases hit CUDA OOM because another job filled the shared GPU; all three pass individually on this branch and on `main`. All `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` cases pass.
3. **Default for FP8 KV.** Agreed, this should stay opt-in until there is a broader sweep. It also overlaps with your #44544 (`ROCM_AITER_ASM` as the gfx950 default for FP8 KV). I think the two can coexist as separate backends:
   - `ROCM_AITER_ASM` consumes the FP8 KV cache directly.
   - This one quantizes the BF16 Q/K/V dynamically per tensor, so it doesn't depend on the KV cache dtype.

   If it helps decide the default, I can run a same-image sweep of FA, ASM and FlyDSL-FP8 (ISL 1k/8k/32k+, concurrency 8–256, plus the Kimi-K3 agentic replay) once #44544 is rebased.

Three technical suggestions:

1. The quantizer grid uses the largest tensor size. V is smaller, so masked threads can still form out-of-range pointers. Please clamp indices or use separate grids.

2. The quantizer allocates temporary buffers on every call. Reusing fixed buffers could reduce the ~50 µs overhead for short inputs.

3. Please disable the ASM FP8 prefill path directly when this backend is selected, instead of relying only on missing metadata to bypass it.

Keeping this opt-in makes sense: short prefills show little benefit, while FP8 accuracy needs a wider long-context evaluation.

@ChuanLi1101 Thanks for the careful read — points 1 and 3 are fixed in 19a77e3, and I have numbers for point 2.

**1. Out-of-range pointers in the shared quant grid**

You're right that the grid is sized for the largest input, so programs can land past the end of a smaller one. Every load and store was already masked and the offset math is int64, so nothing was dereferenced or wrapped — but those programs still computed addresses they had no business computing. Both kernels now stop before that:

- `_partial_amax` derives its trip count per program, `tl.cdiv(N - start, PARTS * BLOCK)`, which is 0 once the program's stripe starts past the end of this input. It still stores its (zero) partial, which the reduce needs.
- `_quant` guards the body with `if start < N or start == 0`. Program 0 stays alive unconditionally so an empty input still gets its descale written.

I added `test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_covers_every_element` to the kernel test: it plants the global max at `{0, BLOCK-1, BLOCK, STRIPE-1, STRIPE, numel-1}` for sizes straddling the 4096-element block and 1048576-element stripe boundaries, up to 3,145,735 elements. It fails if a single element is dropped (verified by shrinking the amax loop to one stripe). The change is perf-neutral: host 46.3–46.8 µs, e2e 349.2 µs at 65K tokens, same as before.

**2. Per-call temporary buffers**

I measured this on MI355X before changing it, since the buffers are tiny (`partial` is 3×256 f32, `scales` is 3 f32). Host cost of `fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(q, k, v)`:

| Variant | Host | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|
| current (5 allocations) | 46.6 µs | — |
| reuse `partial` only | 44.2 µs | −2.4 µs |
| reuse `partial` + `scales` | 42.7 µs | −3.9 µs |
| one merged scratch allocation | 46.7 µs | +0.1 µs |

Where the 46.6 µs goes: 28 µs is the two Triton launches (an empty kernel with the same signature already costs 15.2 µs), 10.2 µs is `torch.empty` ×5, and the rest is the Python wrapper. So the ceiling on reuse is ~8% of host cost and ~1% of the 349 µs e2e at 65K tokens. The three FP8 outputs can't be reused at all — they are returned and stay live for the whole attention call.

Reusing `scales` specifically has a correctness trap: the backend keeps `self._q_fp8 = (q, q_fp8, q_descale)` across the forward, where `q_descale` is a view into that call's `scales`, and each context chunk then calls the quantizer again for its own K/V. A shared per-instance `scales` would be overwritten under the still-live `q_descale` unless keyed by tensor count — exactly the kind of implicit invariant that breaks later.

Given ~2 µs for the only unambiguously safe part (`partial`, which never escapes the function) against making a pure function stateful, I left it as is. Happy to add the `partial` cache if you'd still prefer it — it's a five-line change.

**3. Disabling the ASM FP8 prefill directly**

Agreed, keying off absent PS metadata was too indirect. There's now a single predicate in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`:

```python
def _asm_fp8_prefill_superseded(prefill_backend: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(prefill_backend, AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend)
```

used in both places so they can't drift:

- `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` folds it into `_fp8_prefill_enabled`, so the PS workspace buffers aren't allocated either.
- `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mha` checks the actual `prefill_metadata.prefill_backend` instance and defers to the parent, instead of inferring it from `fp8_prefill_qo_indptr is None`.

`test_mla_backends.py::test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` covers this through the `context_free_prefill` spec.

**4. Opt-in**

Agreed — it stays out of the ROCm auto-selection priorities and is only reachable via `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`.
